review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–51). It has six theorems. Each one proves a single Boolean audit fact (`branchClaimRootValidB ... = true` or `nodeClaimChunkValidB ... = true`) with the one-line proof `decide +kernel`. The theorems differ only in their concrete arguments: branch, row and chunk start and size. The repeated part is a tactic call, not mathematical reasoning that could move into a shared lemma. Any shared helper would have to be a thin wrapper around the existing validity predicates, or would be a different way of splitting the computation. Neither counts as a real finding under this rubric. I did not open the data files or the predicate definitions. I found nothing that justifies a refactor, though I did not check the upstream chunking scheme.
